name: Hverfjall crater and Dimmuborgir
region: East shore of Lake Mývatn, North Iceland
why: Up the black tephra cone of Hverfjall, along the rim of a crater a kilometre wide with Mývatn below, then down across the lava to the dark castles of Dimmuborgir.
book: Free. One way: leave a car at Dimmuborgir, or walk back the same way; the marked path also goes on north to Reykjahlíð. Do not walk into the crater bowl: it is closed to stop erosion.
water: None on the crater: carry 1 litre. Kaffi Borgir café at Dimmuborgir.
dangers: Wind on the open rim, and loose tephra on the steep south descent.
Hidden cracks in the Dimmuborgir lava: stay on the marked paths.
Midges by the lake in June and July: a head net helps.
turnaround: Gale on the rim: walk back down the north path to the car park.

points.name: Hverfjall car park
points.note: At the end of the Hverfjallsvegur track, below the north side of the cone; path HV 1 zigzags straight up.

points.name: Hverfjall crater rim
points.note: The rim, about 140 m above the crater floor: a ring of black tephra 1 km across, Mývatn and the lava fields all round.

points.name: South rim of Hverfjall
points.note: Walk the rim clockwise to the south side, where path HV 2 drops steeply towards the lava.

points.name: Dimmuborgir
points.note: The 'dark castles': lava pillars, arches and caves such as Kirkjan, the 'church'. Short marked loops lead to the car park and café.
